```{r, include = FALSE}
has_arrow <- requireNamespace( "arrow", quietly = TRUE ) &&
             requireNamespace( "data.table", quietly = TRUE )
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>",
  eval     = has_arrow
)
```

npcompete can build every metric for any set of years from a local
**archive**: a panel of Form 990 and 990-EZ filers stored as Parquet files,
one folder per tax year. The archive is built once from the NCCS SOI panel
sample frame (about 2 GB as CSV, 7 million organization-years). After that,
a build only reads the years it needs.

This article walks through the steps on a small stand-in for the full
panel: the Vermont 501(c)(3) filers in `npo_panel_sample` (2015-2019),
written out in the SOI panel layout. With the real file, the steps and
function calls are the same, but builds take minutes instead of seconds.

The archive needs the **arrow** and **data.table** packages.

```{r setup}
library( npcompete )
```

## 1. Set where the archive lives

The archive should live outside the package and outside any synced folder
that might hold files online only. Point npcompete at it once per session,
or set the `NPCOMPETE_ARCHIVE` environment variable in `.Renviron`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options( npcompete.archive_dir = "D:/data/npcompete-archive" )
```

Here we use a temporary folder.

```{r}
arch <- file.path( tempdir(), "npcompete-archive" )
options( npcompete.archive_dir = arch )
```

## 2. Build the archive

`npc_build_archive()` reads the SOI panel CSV, maps its columns to the
package's standard layout with `npc_standardize()`, and writes one Parquet
file per tax year. With the full panel you would run:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
npc_build_archive( "SOI-PANEL-SAMPLE-FRAME-COLUMNS-AUGMENTED-W-POP.CSV" )
```

`npo_panel_sample` lacks a few columns of the full panel (source file,
e-file flag, fiscal year end, revocation dates), so for this example we
add them before writing the CSV.

```{r}
soi <- npo_panel_sample
soi$SOURCE  <- ifelse( is.na( soi$TOTREV ), "", paste0( "SOI_", soi$TAXYEAR + 1, "_PC" ) )
soi$EFILE_X <- "EFILE"
soi$revocation_date <- ""
soi$exemption_reinstatement_date <- ""
soi$TOTLIA  <- NA
soi$REVINVE <- NA
soi$FISYEAR <- soi$TAXYEAR
soi$FISMO   <- 12

csv <- file.path( tempdir(), "soi-panel-vermont.csv" )
data.table::fwrite( soi, csv )

npc_build_archive( csv, overwrite = TRUE )
```

The archive records what it holds. `npc_archive_info()` returns the build
manifest and the rows per tax year, with a flag for years that look
incomplete. In the full panel, the most recent tax year is always partial,
because many organizations have not yet filed. `npc_build_metrics()` drops
flagged years unless you ask it not to.

```{r}
info <- npc_archive_info()
info$year_counts
```

Each organization appears once per tax year. Where the source panel repeats
an organization within a year (a short-period return after a change of
accounting period, or the same return in two extracts), `npc_standardize()`
keeps one filing: the latest extract, then the latest period end.

## 3. Read organizations for some years

`npc_get_orgs()` reads only the requested years. It keeps 501(c)(3)
organizations by default (`subsection = 3`). It also adds `CBSA_FIPS` from
the county-to-CBSA crosswalk (2023 delineation), so every year uses the
same metro boundaries.

```{r}
orgs <- npc_get_orgs( 2018:2019 )
dim( orgs )
head( orgs[ c( "EIN2", "YEAR", "COUNTY_FIPS", "CBSA_FIPS", "NTEEV2",
               "FILER_TYPE", "TOTREV" ) ] )
```

Rows marked `IMPUTED` fill a gap year between two filings: the organization
existed but did not file that year. They count toward organization counts
but carry no financial data. Drop them with `include_imputed = FALSE`.

## 4. Build metrics

`npc_build_metrics()` reads the years, attaches market populations from
`pop_county` and `pop_cbsa`, and computes each requested metric for each
market (CBSA or county), subsector (NTEE major group) and year. It also
reports `SUB = "ALL"` and `GEO = "ALL"` rollups. `npc_metrics()` lists
every metric.

```{r}
npc_metrics()[ c( "id", "family", "by_resource" ) ]
```

The default output is one long table, with one row per market, subsector,
year, resource and metric:

```{r}
m <- npc_build_metrics( 2016:2019, geo = "county",
                        resources = c( "TOTREV", "NETASS" ),
                        metrics = c( "HHI", "CR4", "GINI", "DENSITY_PER_100K",
                                     "DENSITY_PCTL_N" ) )
vt <- substr( m$GEO, 1, 2 ) == "50"     # every US county is in the frame; show Vermont
head( m[ vt, ] )
```

Metrics that do not depend on a resource, such as density, appear once with
`RESOURCE = NA`.

Here is concentration of revenue in Chittenden County (Burlington) across
all subsectors:

```{r}
subset( m, GEO == "50007" & SUB == "ALL" & METRIC %in% c( "HHI", "CR4" ) &
           RESOURCE == "TOTREV" )
```

### Wide tables

`format = "wide"` returns one table per geography and resource, with
metrics as columns. This is the layout of `get_all_metrics()` and of the
files the dashboard reads.

```{r}
w <- npc_build_metrics( 2019, geo = "cbsa", resources = "TOTREV",
                        metrics = c( "HHI", "NHHI", "KWOKA", "DENSITY_PCTL_N" ),
                        format = "wide" )
names( w )
t <- w$cbsa_TOTREV
subset( t, SUB == "ALL" & N > 0 )
```

In this sample `DENSITY_PCTL_N` sits at its cap of 2 for every Vermont
metro. The density model compares each market with every other market in
the country, and in this sample only Vermont has any organizations. With
the full panel, values spread around 0.

### Pooled windows for small markets

Small markets have few organizations, so their metrics jump from year to
year. `window = 3` pools three years for each reported year:

- each organization's financial values are averaged over the years it
  appears;
- its location and subsector come from its latest year;
- population is the three-year average.

Reported years without a full window of data are dropped.

```{r}
w3 <- npc_build_metrics( 2017:2019, geo = "county", window = 3,
                         metrics = c( "DENSITY_PER_100K", "MEDIAN_AGE" ),
                         format = "wide" )
subset( w3$county, SUB == "ALL" & substr( GEO, 1, 2 ) == "50" & YEAR == 2019 )
```

### Writing results with a manifest

With `out_dir`, the results are written as CSV along with `manifest.csv`.
The manifest records the archive used, the years, metrics, options and
package version, so the build can be reproduced or compared with a later
one.

```{r}
out <- file.path( tempdir(), "metrics" )
res <- npc_build_metrics( 2018:2019, geo = "cbsa", resources = "TOTREV",
                          metrics = c( "HHI", "GINI" ), format = "wide",
                          out_dir = out )
list.files( out )
head( attr( res, "manifest" ), 12 )
```

## Choices that change the results

- **`cbsa`**: `"crosswalk"` (default) assigns CBSAs from each county under
  the 2023 delineation, the same boundaries as the population data.
  `"geocode"` uses the CBSA assigned when the address was geocoded, which
  reproduces tables built before this option existed.
- **`subsection`**: 501(c)(3) only by default; `NULL` keeps every
  subsection.
- **`density_model`**: the count model behind `DENSITY_PCTL_N`, negative
  binomial by default (see `vignette("density")`).
- **`drop_incomplete_years`**: keep partial years only when you know why
  you want them.

To build the same metrics without the SOI panel, from public NCCS files,
see `vignette("build-from-nccs")`.
